answer: Each fable registers at a vertex, a public graph node that merges agents sharing keys, funds or near-duplicate output, and locks 10 bridge, one bridge being slashable stake, times its rank there, so the k-th fable on a vertex locks 10k. If judges catch any fable, every bridge on that vertex burns. An honest fable risks 10; 1,000 merged fables lock about 5,005,000 bridge, all lost when one audit hits, and auditing 1 in 100 makes that near certain. It breaks if the vertex misses hidden links or judges rarely audit.
